newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-O'MEARA AND STRANGE, BECK AND HOCH TIED AT SHARK SHOOTOUT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-O'MEARA AND STRANGE, BECK AND HOCH TIED AT SHARK SHOOTOUT.

text.p: The teams of
Mark O'Meara and Curtis Strange and Chip Beck and Scott Hoch
fired 6-under-par 66s Friday to share the lead after the
first-round alternate shot competition at the $1.1 million
Shark Shootout Friday.
Greg Norman, who has never won the tournament he hosts,
teamed with two-time champion Raymond Floyd to card a 67. The
Norman-Floyd team is tied for second with the duos of John
Daly and David Duval and Jay Haas and Tom Kite.
O'Meara and Strange, who had a bogey-free round, started
the round strong, birdying the first two holes and adding a
35-foot birdie putt from O'Meara on the par-4, 449-yard
seventh hole.
The duo continued to blister the course on the back nine,
adding birdies on the 10th, 15th and 16th holes.
"We played solid," said Strange. "Six-under is a good
round in alternate shot. If you get behind today, it's tough
to catch up."
"If we play our game under control, we can do good
things," added O'Meara. "We now can go out with less pressure
and play our game. I know Curtis is giving his best and he
knows I am too."
Beck and Hoch also began the round with three birdies on
the front nine, including one by Hoch from 25 feet on the
seventh hole. After parring the next five holes, Beck sank a
tap-in birdie putt on 13 before the duo recorded its only
bogey on 14.
However, the team bounced back quickly with a birdie on
15 and an eagle on the par-5, 537-yard 16th hole.
"If I look back at how we played, we are fortunate to be
6-under," Hoch said. "We could have been much better. We did
pretty much everything well, except Chip drove it poorly.
Fortunately for us, I drove it well. I kind of wanted it
different, because Chip putts so well."
Brad Faxon and Peter Jacobsen are tied with the tandem of
Hale Irwin and Lee Janzen for sixth at 4-under.
Defending champions Steve Elkington and Mark Calcavecchia
combined for a 69, along with Craig Stadler and Lanny
Wadkins.
The Sherwood Country Club course is a par-72, 7,025-yard
layout. First prize is $150,000 for each person.
